sentences.text: Ms. Anushri Chourasiya - Advocate for appellant

. 
 Ms. Amit Pandey - Government Advocate for respondent/Stat Heard on IA No.26747/2025, which is an application filed under Section 430(1) of BNSS, 2023 on behalf of the appellant for grant of bail and suspension of remaining jail sentence.

Appellant is facing sentence by virtue of judgment dated 30.09.2015 passed by the First Additional Sessions Judge, Satna in Special Case No.58/2013 whereby the appellant has been convicted for offences under Sections 342/34 and 376 (d) of IPC and sentenced to undergo 1 Year R.I. and 20 Year R.I. with fine of Rs.1,000/- and Rs.10,000/-.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the co-accused has been granted the benefit of suspension of the remaining jail sentence.
In the present case, there is no FSL report.
The medical examination was conducted 5-6 days after the incident.
From the statement of the victim, it prima facie appears that no rape has been committed upon her.
The doctor has not expressed any definite opinion regarding rape.
The appellant is about 21 years of age.

This appeal pertains to the year 2015,
and the final conclusion is likely to take sufficient time.
The appellant has already undergone more than 10 years of imprisonment.

In light of the judgment of the Apex Court in Saudan Singh v. State of U.P. [SLP (Crl.) No. 4633/2021, decided on 2 CRA-2931-2015 05.10.2021], it is submitted that the remaining jail sentence of the appellant may be suspended until the final disposal of this appeal.

entities.text: Saudan Singh v. State of U.P. [SLP (Crl.) No. 4633/2021
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/State opposes the application for suspension of sentence on the ground that there are serious allegations against the appellant therefore, the present application deserves to be dismissed.

Considering the reasons stated in the application coupled with the fact that appellant has completed more than 10 years of jail incarceration and that final conclusion of this appeal will take considerable long time, we deem it appropriate to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the Pankaj Saket vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37404125/
1 appellant.
Accordingly, IA No.26747/2025 is allowed and the execution of remaining jail sentence of the appellant is hereby suspended till the final disposal of this appeal.

entities.text: Pankaj Saket vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is directed that appellant be released on bail subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited and upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.15,000/- (Rupees Fifteen Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, with a further direction to appear before the Registry of this Court on 15.04.2026 and on such other dates, as may be fixed by the Registry of this Court in this regard during the pendency of this appeal.
List for hearing in due course.
